system_summary: A conditional system for deciding, producing, assuring and evolving related products through warranted commonality, controlled variability and feedback. The coupled loops are constrained by product obligations, evidence boundaries, legitimate authority and lifecycle economics; technique branches are alternatives, not a forced serial pipeline.

nodes.NAME: Warranted family scoping
nodes.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: relational reconstruction grounded in the cited mechanisms; not a newly proved or academically standard unified model.
nodes.STATE: Let P be candidate products, N(p) their needs and A(p) their domain assumptions. A scope S is a selected subset with explicit exclusions, expected demand and candidate common assets. Similarity of names or files is evidence to investigate, not the membership predicate.
nodes.OPERATION: Compare products and counterexamples; identify which assumptions can be common and which require variation. Estimate the burden of the resulting family and compare an adequate non-family alternative. A contradiction may split S, keep a product local or reject the family proposal. Scope can be revised from product feedback.

nodes.NAME: Domain/application feedback and decision responsibility
nodes.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: relational reconstruction grounded in the cited mechanisms; not a newly proved or academically standard unified model.
nodes.STATE: Domain state contains assets, constraints and production knowledge; application state contains requested/realised products, local differences and observations. Responsibility for these states may be held by the same people.
nodes.OPERATION: Product requests and failures flow to asset maintainers with baseline context. Maintainers may revise a core asset or model, decline generalisation, retain an exception or reopen scope. New core releases return constraints and evidence to products. Work can proceed concurrently on compatible baselines; conflicts require a decision rather than an automatic merge.

nodes.NAME: Feature and constraint semantics
nodes.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: relational reconstruction grounded in the cited mechanisms; not a newly proved or academically standard unified model.
nodes.STATE: For Boolean features F and encoded constraints φ, Cφ = {c in {0,1}^F | φ(c)}. Richer models replace Boolean valuations with typed domains. Domain-valid choices Cdomain need not equal Cφ. A feature interpretation links selections to stakeholder meaning.
nodes.OPERATION: Check satisfiability, forced/dead options and conflicts; explain actionable repairs; validate accepted and rejected combinations against domain evidence. Translation or model evolution uses explicit feature correspondence rather than names alone.

nodes.NAME: Variability realisation and binding
nodes.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: relational reconstruction grounded in the cited mechanisms; not a newly proved or academically standard unified model.
nodes.STATE: M is a possibly many-to-many relation between features, artefact fragments and variation points. Each variation point has a resolution stage. A product transformation D consumes asset versions, configuration and relevant tool/environment inputs.
nodes.OPERATION: Choose conditional selection, parameters, modules, plugins/inheritance, aspects, deltas or generators according to the variation. Deltas require applicable ordered transformations; annotated systems require faithful presence conditions. Late binding carries additional runtime state and transition obligations.

nodes.NAME: Asset and derivation provenance
nodes.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: relational reconstruction grounded in the cited mechanisms; not a newly proved or academically standard unified model.
nodes.STATE: A product identity includes relevant model/configuration, core assets, generator/build/dependency versions, consequential environment inputs and the resulting artefact identity. The needed equivalence relation may be semantic, structural or byte-level.
nodes.OPERATION: Execute a version-related production plan, record or retain the inputs needed for the declared reconstruction claim and validate output at the relevant level. Reference architectures supply enforceable obligations only where the real process checks or constrains conformance.

nodes.NAME: Configuration-space assurance
nodes.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: relational reconstruction grounded in the cited mechanisms; not a newly proved or academically standard unified model.
nodes.STATE: The relevant space is Ω = configurations × ordinary inputs × environments × baselines, restricted by actual obligations. An analysis or test covers a declared subset or property of Ω. A model check, a parser and a behavioural test have different objects.
nodes.OPERATION: Select product-based, feature/compositional, family-based or hybrid analysis. Reuse results only with checked premises. Sampling trades execution cost against omitted cases; known interactions can justify risk-directed additions. Shared failures interrupt the normal derivation path and trigger impact analysis.

nodes.NAME: Family evolution, migration and retirement
nodes.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: relational reconstruction grounded in the cited mechanisms; not a newly proved or academically standard unified model.
nodes.STATE: At baseline k the family has model φk, assets Ak, supported product identities Pk and evidence Ek. A migration m maps old products/selections to new ones with explicit feature correspondence and intent. Legacy admission to new products is distinct from support of old ones.
nodes.OPERATION: Classify model differences, identify shared-asset impact, select migration or parallel support, update tests and accept actual products. Extracted constraints can repair a stale model only after domain reconciliation. Retirement may first forbid new selection while preserving older baselines.

nodes.NAME: Organisational economics and external constraints
nodes.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: relational reconstruction grounded in the cited mechanisms; not a newly proved or academically standard unified model.
nodes.STATE: For an explicit horizon compare SPL cost = organisational transition + core assets + product derivation + assurance + coordination + support/migration/exit with equivalent-outcome alternatives. These are cost categories, not measured universal coefficients. Authority and external obligations constrain admissible alternatives before cost ranking.
nodes.OPERATION: Use scenarios and observed product experience to revisit investment, team capacity, exceptions and scope. Negotiate with external participants where there is no internal authority. A shared specification ecosystem is not automatically one product-production organisation.

nodes.NAME: Dynamic configuration transitions and learned proposals
nodes.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: relational reconstruction grounded in the cited mechanisms; not a newly proved or academically standard unified model.
nodes.STATE: A dynamic state is (c,s,e): feature selection, operational state and relevant environment. Edges represent feasible actions with guards, effects and controllability. A learned proposal is an input to checking, not an edge that is automatically authorised.
nodes.OPERATION: Observe context, propose a permitted target, check a feasible safe path, execute authorised actions and observe the result. A safe offline phase or actual atomic transfer can justify transitions otherwise unsafe, but cannot be assumed. Model/tool changes require re-establishing the guarantees they affect.

alternative_configurations.NAME: Small stable family with mostly manual derivation
alternative_configurations.SELECTION: Repeated related products, modest variation, stable obligations and a credible cost case.

alternative_configurations.OMIT: Do not require a dedicated platform team, SAT solver, feature language, automatic generator or runtime supervisor.
alternative_configurations.RETIRE: Return to selective reuse or independent products if support and coordination cease to earn their cost.

alternative_configurations.NAME: Large static or generated family
alternative_configurations.SELECTION: Configuration complexity or repeated production makes formal diagnostics, generation or shared analysis worthwhile.
alternative_configurations.MECHANISM: Choose complementary diagnostics, analysis and sampling under a common model/realisation/acceptance boundary.
alternative_configurations.OMIT: No obligation to use all three analysis strategies; unsupported or low-value techniques are excluded.
alternative_configurations.RETIRE: Remove a specialised tool when supported products and analysis needs no longer justify it.

alternative_configurations.NAME: Extractive or incrementally consolidated portfolio
alternative_configurations.SELECTION: Existing variants have useful commonality but cannot immediately move to one maintained core.
alternative_configurations.MECHANISM: Recover differences and provenance; review with domain experts; consolidate selectively while keeping justified exceptions and supported baselines.
alternative_configurations.OMIT: Do not require immediate eradication of every clone or a complete future feature model.
alternative_configurations.RETIRE: Stop consolidation where expected savings do not exceed semantic recovery and migration burden.

alternative_configurations.NAME: Dynamic product line
alternative_configurations.SELECTION: Runtime variation responds to a specified operational need rather than generic flexibility.
alternative_configurations.MECHANISM: Permitted states plus context observations and a transition protocol; supervisory synthesis only when its model and control assumptions fit.
alternative_configurations.OMIT: Do not infer safe transitions from valid endpoints, and do not require dynamic machinery for static families.
alternative_configurations.RETIRE: Prefer earlier binding when runtime benefit disappears or operational assurance cannot be justified.

alternative_configurations.NAME: Inter-organisational or community arrangement
alternative_configurations.SELECTION: Independent owners share compatibility or platform interests but lack a single common-core authority.

alternative_configurations.OMIT: Do not assume this is identical to one organisation deriving all products from one core.
alternative_configurations.RETIRE: Reduce shared coordination where no interoperability or shared-asset obligation remains.

domain_models.NAME: Warranted family scoping
domain_models.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: relational reconstruction grounded in the cited mechanisms; not a newly proved or academically standard unified model.
domain_models.PURPOSE: Determine whether and where joint product production is technically meaningful and economically worth considering.
domain_models.OBJECTS_AND_STATE: Let P be candidate products, N(p) their needs and A(p) their domain assumptions. A scope S is a selected subset with explicit exclusions, expected demand and candidate common assets. Similarity of names or files is evidence to investigate, not the membership predicate.
domain_models.OPERATION_AND_DECISIONS: Compare products and counterexamples; identify which assumptions can be common and which require variation. Estimate the burden of the resulting family and compare an adequate non-family alternative. A contradiction may split S, keep a product local or reject the family proposal. Scope can be revised from product feedback.
domain_models.OBSERVATIONS_AND_POSTCONDITIONS: The decision records included/excluded products, common assumptions, intended variation and what demand or contradiction would reopen it. Economic adequacy is a separate judgement, not proved by the existence of S.
domain_models.LIMITS_AND_CHEAP_FORM: A small comparison table and direct expert review can be enough. No similarity threshold or universal break-even count is inferred.

domain_models.NAME: Domain/application feedback and decision responsibility
domain_models.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: relational reconstruction grounded in the cited mechanisms; not a newly proved or academically standard unified model.
domain_models.PURPOSE: Keep reusable capability development connected to actual product production without forcing a serial lifecycle.
domain_models.OBJECTS_AND_STATE: Domain state contains assets, constraints and production knowledge; application state contains requested/realised products, local differences and observations. Responsibility for these states may be held by the same people.
domain_models.OPERATION_AND_DECISIONS: Product requests and failures flow to asset maintainers with baseline context. Maintainers may revise a core asset or model, decline generalisation, retain an exception or reopen scope. New core releases return constraints and evidence to products. Work can proceed concurrently on compatible baselines; conflicts require a decision rather than an automatic merge.
domain_models.OBSERVATIONS_AND_POSTCONDITIONS: Every consequential feedback item has a consumer and a disposition; product builders can identify the baseline and limits they inherit. Observing a problem, being able/authorised to change it and establishing the result are separate steps.
domain_models.LIMITS_AND_CHEAP_FORM: Use direct coordination in a small family. No new team, meeting ritual or autonomous controller follows from the model.

domain_models.NAME: Feature and constraint semantics
domain_models.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: relational reconstruction grounded in the cited mechanisms; not a newly proved or academically standard unified model.
domain_models.PURPOSE: Describe permitted selections and the meaning needed to use them in product decisions.
domain_models.OBJECTS_AND_STATE: For Boolean features F and encoded constraints φ, Cφ = {c in {0,1}^F | φ(c)}. Richer models replace Boolean valuations with typed domains. Domain-valid choices Cdomain need not equal Cφ. A feature interpretation links selections to stakeholder meaning.
domain_models.OPERATION_AND_DECISIONS: Check satisfiability, forced/dead options and conflicts; explain actionable repairs; validate accepted and rejected combinations against domain evidence. Translation or model evolution uses explicit feature correspondence rather than names alone.
domain_models.OBSERVATIONS_AND_POSTCONDITIONS: A SAT witness establishes membership of Cφ, not membership of Cdomain without adequacy evidence and not correctness of an implementation. An anomaly is a diagnostic to interpret, not automatically an error.
domain_models.LIMITS_AND_CHEAP_FORM: Use explicit enumeration or a decision table when small. Arithmetic, cardinality and typed extensions are optional but must not be discarded silently by tools.

domain_models.NAME: Variability realisation and binding
domain_models.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: relational reconstruction grounded in the cited mechanisms; not a newly proved or academically standard unified model.
domain_models.PURPOSE: Relate domain selections to actual artefacts and determine when unresolved choices become fixed.
domain_models.OBJECTS_AND_STATE: M is a possibly many-to-many relation between features, artefact fragments and variation points. Each variation point has a resolution stage. A product transformation D consumes asset versions, configuration and relevant tool/environment inputs.
domain_models.OPERATION_AND_DECISIONS: Choose conditional selection, parameters, modules, plugins/inheritance, aspects, deltas or generators according to the variation. Deltas require applicable ordered transformations; annotated systems require faithful presence conditions. Late binding carries additional runtime state and transition obligations.
domain_models.OBSERVATIONS_AND_POSTCONDITIONS: A realisation check establishes R(D(A,c,t,e), c): that the produced artefacts realise the intended selection. Successful generation or compilation alone does not establish R or required behaviour.
domain_models.LIMITS_AND_CHEAP_FORM: This equation is an analytical schema, not a universal deterministic generator theorem. A reviewed manual derivation may implement D adequately.

domain_models.NAME: Asset and derivation provenance
domain_models.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: relational reconstruction grounded in the cited mechanisms; not a newly proved or academically standard unified model.
domain_models.PURPOSE: Make a produced product supportable and keep evidence attached to the baseline that actually generated it.
domain_models.OBJECTS_AND_STATE: A product identity includes relevant model/configuration, core assets, generator/build/dependency versions, consequential environment inputs and the resulting artefact identity. The needed equivalence relation may be semantic, structural or byte-level.
domain_models.OPERATION_AND_DECISIONS: Execute a version-related production plan, record or retain the inputs needed for the declared reconstruction claim and validate output at the relevant level. Reference architectures supply enforceable obligations only where the real process checks or constrains conformance.
domain_models.OBSERVATIONS_AND_POSTCONDITIONS: A second builder can reproduce the needed result or explain differences; a failure report can be located in configuration and baseline space. Hash identity cannot establish semantic adequacy.
domain_models.LIMITS_AND_CHEAP_FORM: No universal requirement for byte-for-byte builds or full automation. Retention is scoped to support and assurance needs.

domain_models.NAME: Configuration-space assurance
domain_models.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: relational reconstruction grounded in the cited mechanisms; not a newly proved or academically standard unified model.
domain_models.PURPOSE: Choose and compose evidence without confusing configuration coverage with product correctness.
domain_models.OBJECTS_AND_STATE: The relevant space is Ω = configurations × ordinary inputs × environments × baselines, restricted by actual obligations. An analysis or test covers a declared subset or property of Ω. A model check, a parser and a behavioural test have different objects.
domain_models.OPERATION_AND_DECISIONS: Select product-based, feature/compositional, family-based or hybrid analysis. Reuse results only with checked premises. Sampling trades execution cost against omitted cases; known interactions can justify risk-directed additions. Shared failures interrupt the normal derivation path and trigger impact analysis.
domain_models.OBSERVATIONS_AND_POSTCONDITIONS: Each claim names what is quantified, its oracle and the product identities to which it applies. Conditional static warnings remain warnings unless confirmed; complete configuration coverage does not mean all behaviours were checked.
domain_models.LIMITS_AND_CHEAP_FORM: The smallest adequate form can be all supported products plus targeted tests. Family-wide symbolic work is optional and may lose to ordinary analysis for small families.

domain_models.NAME: Family evolution, migration and retirement
domain_models.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: relational reconstruction grounded in the cited mechanisms; not a newly proved or academically standard unified model.
domain_models.PURPOSE: Preserve or explicitly revise supported product obligations through changes in models, assets and production.
domain_models.OBJECTS_AND_STATE: At baseline k the family has model φk, assets Ak, supported product identities Pk and evidence Ek. A migration m maps old products/selections to new ones with explicit feature correspondence and intent. Legacy admission to new products is distinct from support of old ones.
domain_models.OPERATION_AND_DECISIONS: Classify model differences, identify shared-asset impact, select migration or parallel support, update tests and accept actual products. Extracted constraints can repair a stale model only after domain reconciliation. Retirement may first forbid new selection while preserving older baselines.
domain_models.OBSERVATIONS_AND_POSTCONDITIONS: A migrated product meets the intended preserved obligations or records accepted changes. Ek is not automatically evidence for baseline k+1. Configuration-distance minimisation is not a proof of minimal labour or unchanged behaviour.
domain_models.LIMITS_AND_CHEAP_FORM: Manual migration or a supported old baseline can be adequate. No compulsory simultaneous release or eventual reintegration of every exception.

domain_models.NAME: Organisational economics and external constraints
domain_models.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: relational reconstruction grounded in the cited mechanisms; not a newly proved or academically standard unified model.
domain_models.PURPOSE: Choose a feasible production arrangement while accounting for the parties who bear its costs and obligations.
domain_models.OBJECTS_AND_STATE: For an explicit horizon compare SPL cost = organisational transition + core assets + product derivation + assurance + coordination + support/migration/exit with equivalent-outcome alternatives. These are cost categories, not measured universal coefficients. Authority and external obligations constrain admissible alternatives before cost ranking.
domain_models.OPERATION_AND_DECISIONS: Use scenarios and observed product experience to revisit investment, team capacity, exceptions and scope. Negotiate with external participants where there is no internal authority. A shared specification ecosystem is not automatically one product-production organisation.
domain_models.OBSERVATIONS_AND_POSTCONDITIONS: The decision identifies cost bearers, demand assumptions, omitted costs and conditions that reverse preference. No claimed causal benefit follows merely from adopting a standard or successful organisation.
domain_models.LIMITS_AND_CHEAP_FORM: A coarse comparison can be sufficient; no universal ROI, break-even count or required governance structure is asserted.

domain_models.NAME: Dynamic configuration transitions and learned proposals
domain_models.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: relational reconstruction grounded in the cited mechanisms; not a newly proved or academically standard unified model.
domain_models.PURPOSE: Keep runtime or learned changes inside justified configuration, transition, authority and evidence boundaries.
domain_models.OBJECTS_AND_STATE: A dynamic state is (c,s,e): feature selection, operational state and relevant environment. Edges represent feasible actions with guards, effects and controllability. A learned proposal is an input to checking, not an edge that is automatically authorised.
domain_models.OPERATION_AND_DECISIONS: Observe context, propose a permitted target, check a feasible safe path, execute authorised actions and observe the result. A safe offline phase or actual atomic transfer can justify transitions otherwise unsafe, but cannot be assumed. Model/tool changes require re-establishing the guarantees they affect.
domain_models.OBSERVATIONS_AND_POSTCONDITIONS: Safe endpoints do not prove safe edges. Supervisory nonblocking is reachability of marked states, not inevitable completion. Issuing a command does not establish its effect. Fixed features do not imply fixed environmental behaviour.
domain_models.LIMITS_AND_CHEAP_FORM: Choose static/deployment binding, deterministic migration or advisory-only output when richer operation is not warranted. Physical safety and learned-output generalisation remain assumption-bound.

edges.DOCUMENTARY_BASIS: Both concern related reusable programs; inspected evidence is insufficient to assert direct transmission between these exact works.
Domain analysis and program-family design share the problem of reusable knowledge; this edge does not assert derivation of FODA from one paper alone.
PuLSE explicitly responds to limitations of large, insufficiently product-focused domain-engineering approaches.
Pohl et al. chapter 2 explicitly identifies Weiss and Lai and industrial initiatives among framework antecedents; this is framework-level, not a claim that every operation originated in FAST.
Related industrial product-line practice informs both; different representations preserve coupled product/core responsibilities.
Feature-model analysis papers explicitly formalise and analyse feature-model constraints associated with the FODA lineage.
Delta-oriented programming explicitly addresses expressiveness limitations of additive feature-oriented programming.
Family assurance investigates how feature-oriented and other variability realisations can be analysed without only enumerating products.
Configuration-set semantics become the basis for classifying edits and adapting configurations/tests.
Extraction and feature modelling are applied to existing cloned or industrial variants, subject to missing-domain-knowledge limits.
Feature selection is applied to runtime adaptation; transition behaviour adds obligations beyond static configuration.
The paper explicitly combines product-line dynamic reconfiguration with discrete-event supervisory control and identifies prior approaches it extends.
Bosch explicitly argues for organisational expansion from product lines to ecosystems; the later community taxonomy describes a distinct coordination arrangement.

The 2026 paper explicitly contrasts independently developed interoperable implementations with classical common-core product-line arrangements. This edge records the documented comparison, not an assertion of direct derivation from Bosch alone.
UVL explicitly addresses fragmentation in feature modelling and documents the MODEVAR initiative and language levels.
Learned tools are proposed for evolution/derivation tasks; inspected evidence varies from metadata to exploratory evaluations, so replacement benefit is not established.
New proposals question maintained configuration machinery; this study retains reduction as conditional and regeneration superiority as unresolved.

discriminating_cases.NAME: Three similar products with incompatible assumptions
discriminating_cases.GIVEN: A batch collector tolerates reordering, a controller requires bounded response, and an offline recorder must survive disconnection. All share a serialisation library.
discriminating_cases.SYSTEM_RESPONSE: Do not infer one production family or one scheduler from the library. Test whether a narrow common layer plus explicit variations can meet all assumptions at acceptable cost; split scope if not.
discriminating_cases.DISCRIMINATING_OBSERVATION: A proposed invariant that requires permanent connectivity is contradicted by the recorder. Sharing serialisation remains possible.
discriminating_cases.LIMITS: This does not prove that the three products can never form a family under a different architecture.

discriminating_cases.NAME: Valid feature model, defective generator
discriminating_cases.GIVEN: The model requires exactly one of A or B; configuration A=true,B=false is valid, but the generator emits B.
discriminating_cases.SYSTEM_RESPONSE: Pass encoded consistency, fail the intended realisation relation and withhold product acceptance. Retain configuration and generator identity for diagnosis.
discriminating_cases.DISCRIMINATING_OBSERVATION: The emitted capability disagrees with the selected feature despite successful compilation.
discriminating_cases.LIMITS: The toy oracle checks a simple mapping, not arbitrary product behaviour.

discriminating_cases.NAME: Shared security repair breaks a supported variant
discriminating_cases.GIVEN: A common security repair exceeds the memory budget of one still-supported product.
discriminating_cases.SYSTEM_RESPONSE: Do not claim family-wide completion. Assess differentiated backport, a supportable baseline or an explicit product exception with the relevant decision authority.
discriminating_cases.DISCRIMINATING_OBSERVATION: The repaired high-resource products pass, but the low-resource product fails its acceptance obligation; this result interrupts blanket propagation.
discriminating_cases.LIMITS: No specific vulnerability, legal requirement or acceptable security exception is invented.

discriminating_cases.NAME: Pairwise coverage misses a three-way fault
discriminating_cases.GIVEN: For three unconstrained Boolean features, sample 000,011,101,110. A fault activates only at 111.
discriminating_cases.SYSTEM_RESPONSE: Recognise complete pairwise assignment coverage but no general interaction-correctness guarantee. Add a higher-order test when the risk or interaction hypothesis warrants it.
discriminating_cases.DISCRIMINATING_OBSERVATION: The executable check confirms all 2-variable assignments occur and 111 is absent.
discriminating_cases.LIMITS: This counterexample disproves the universal completeness inference; it does not show pairwise testing is useless.

discriminating_cases.NAME: Safe endpoints, unsafe transition
discriminating_cases.GIVEN: Exactly one provider must be active. Endpoints (1,0) and (0,1) are safe; the platform only changes one Boolean variable at a time.
discriminating_cases.SYSTEM_RESPONSE: No safe path exists under those actions. Require a genuinely atomic transfer, a separately specified safe quiescent protocol, or reject the transition.
discriminating_cases.DISCRIMINATING_OBSERVATION: Enumerating the one-bit graph shows both intermediate states (0,0) and (1,1) violate the invariant.
discriminating_cases.LIMITS: An atomic or quiescent mechanism cannot be assumed merely to make the model work.

discriminating_cases.NAME: Small portfolio where cloning is adequate
discriminating_cases.GIVEN: Hypothetical equivalent obligations: a two-product clone-and-own route costs 60 effort units over the decision horizon; establishing and operating the family costs 120. Estimates already include the stated support work.
discriminating_cases.SYSTEM_RESPONSE: Select the lower-cost adequate alternative and revisit the decision if demand, propagation or support assumptions change.
discriminating_cases.DISCRIMINATING_OBSERVATION: 60 < 120 under the declared scenario; no product-count threshold is inferred.
discriminating_cases.LIMITS: The values are invented to test the decision rule, not estimates from an industrial study.

discriminating_cases.NAME: A favourable modest static family
discriminating_cases.GIVEN: Several metering products share stable measurement semantics and differ in a declared display and communication option. A maintained library and deployment-time parameter file realise those differences.
discriminating_cases.SYSTEM_RESPONSE: Use a small decision table, versioned assets/configuration, a repeatable derivation instruction and appropriate product checks. No runtime supervisor or feature DSL is required.
discriminating_cases.DISCRIMINATING_OBSERVATION: Derived products satisfy their declared measurement and interface obligations; actual saved work can be compared with maintained alternatives.
discriminating_cases.LIMITS: Technical coherence in this invented example is not empirical proof of return on investment.

discriminating_cases.NAME: The actuator command is not the observed transition
discriminating_cases.GIVEN: A controller issues a reconfiguration command, but the state observer is stale and the physical action may have failed.
discriminating_cases.SYSTEM_RESPONSE: Do not equate a decision, permission or issued command with achieved state. Use warranted feedback or enter the explicitly designed failure response.
discriminating_cases.DISCRIMINATING_OBSERVATION: Independent current state evidence is missing, so the transition postcondition is not established.
discriminating_cases.LIMITS: The study does not prescribe a universal safe fallback for every plant.

discriminating_cases.NAME: A changed assurance assumption
discriminating_cases.GIVEN: A family-analysis result assumed a particular build constraint, but a generator upgrade changes which module is included.
discriminating_cases.SYSTEM_RESPONSE: Invalidate or narrow the inherited result until model/implementation correspondence is re-established; do not carry the old guarantee solely because feature names match.
discriminating_cases.DISCRIMINATING_OBSERVATION: The represented configuration no longer matches the built product.
discriminating_cases.LIMITS: This is an analytical obligation derived from assurance boundaries, not a reported incident.

discriminating_cases.NAME: Industrial global model becomes stale
discriminating_cases.GIVEN: The Bosch PS-EC report describes formerly used high-level feature models becoming outdated and falling out of use, and studies dependencies across seven selected projects.
discriminating_cases.SYSTEM_RESPONSE: Retain maintainable, subsystem-aligned models with domain review and cross-boundary consistency, rather than demand one comprehensive central model.
discriminating_cases.DISCRIMINATING_OBSERVATION: The report documents maintenance and extraction limits; it does not establish a controlled ROI comparison for the proposed model organisation.
discriminating_cases.LIMITS: One family and purposive project selection; not a universal failure rate.

discriminating_cases.NAME: Configuration-dependent generator failures
discriminating_cases.GIVEN: The historical JHipster study reports 9,376 failed configurations out of 26,256 in Results §6.1, with a minor denominator discrepancy elsewhere.
discriminating_cases.SYSTEM_RESPONSE: Treat feature/configuration validity and generated-product outcomes separately; use the reported fault interactions to judge sampling limits in that version.
discriminating_cases.DISCRIMINATING_OBSERVATION: The study reports six faults including a higher-order interaction, not a general defect rate for all configurable generators.
discriminating_cases.LIMITS: One historical version; infrastructure/configuration conditions and the paper denominator discrepancy are retained.

relation_semantics.REQUIRES: FROM cannot establish its stated bounded claim without TO, under the guard; this does not mandate either technique outside that guard.
relation_semantics.CONSTRAINS: FROM restricts the interpretation or admissible operation of TO; it need not be a temporal predecessor.
relation_semantics.ENABLES: FROM makes TO feasible or informative without proving its consequence.
relation_semantics.PROVIDES_EVIDENCE_FOR: FROM supplies bounded evidence to TO, not an unconditional guarantee.
relation_semantics.COMMUNICATES_TO: Results from FROM are delivered to a responsible consumer of TO; delivery, authority and achieved outcome remain distinct.
relation_semantics.ACTS_THROUGH: FROM is made operative through the selected TO mechanisms.
relation_semantics.FEEDBACK_TO: Observations or changed assumptions in FROM can revise TO.
relation_semantics.ALTERNATIVE_TO: Guarded alternative approaches, not necessarily alternatives to their common evaluation criterion.
relation_semantics.CONFLICTS_WITH: The overclaim or assumption in FROM cannot be combined unqualified with TO under the guard.
relation_semantics.REFINES: FROM adds a narrower or stronger obligation to the distinction in TO.
relation_semantics.UNUSED_TYPES: SUPERSEDES and SHARES_ANCESTRY_WITH are available vocabulary, but no property-level universal replacement or additional ancestry edge is asserted merely to populate a type; genealogy has its own documentary edge classification.
